newsitem.title: USA: Scandinavian acceptance of EDI waybills nears 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Scandinavian acceptance of EDI waybills nears 50 pct.

text.p: Almost half of air cargo airwaybills in Scandinavia now are filed electronically, an International Air Transport Association (IATA) Cargo Week 97 workshop was told.
Last year, over 480,000 electronic waybills were filed out of about 1 million, consultant Roland Hallfors said at the workshop on Electronic Document Interchange(EDI).
That is more than three times the worldwide average for EDI transmission of waybill information in the air cargo sector, and more than five times the U.S. rate.

Hallfors, from the London-based Desima Marketing Ltd provided consultancy services for the Scandinavian cargo information system, TradeVision. He told the workshop that each electronic waybill costs about two dollars to generate, or five dollars less than a paper waybill.

Hallfors said that at the current rate electronic waybills are being used, that generates about $2.6 million in theoretical savings a year for Scandinavian carriers and about $2.84 million for forwarders.

He said the high rate of acceptance for EDI in Scandinavia includes such factors as the choice of interface options provided and the extensive training TradeVision offers operators at freight forwarders.
Also, SAS, the Scandinavian flag carrier, rebates about one dollar per electronic transaction as an incentive to avoid paper-based transactions, he added.
Sixty percent of SAS waybills are now electronic, he said.

Hallfors added that while TradeVision launched an Internet-based interface last year, it should not eclipse TradeVision's closed booking system due to concerns some forwarders have over the reliability and security of internet links.
